Question: Can someone be a successful music teacher without being proficient in playing an instrument or singing?
Answer: That actually describes a student teacher I had. She failed her first placement (elementary), I failed her, and she had to double up (elementary AND Upper grades)for a 3rd semester before she could even muster a C in student teaching. She had no business leading a music ensemble, ever.

Question: Is it acceptable for students to correct their teachers? What are the potential reasons for or against this practice?
Answer: During graduate school I had the retired head of the music department for Symphonic Literature and 20th Century Composers. It was during the 20th Century class that he frequently would list dates for the composers, most, though elderly, were alive. Occasionally, one would have recently shaken off their mortal coil. For some reason, I was attuned to these passing. I very respectfully would raise my hand, or speak to him after class to share my information. This dear man, whom I greatly respected, wrote me a most glowing recommendation, calling me respectful without being a suck-up, humorous without being flippant, intelligent without being a know-it-all. I loved that old guy!
